title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways you can climb to the top.
constraints: Each move is either 1 step or 2 steps
The order of steps matters (distinct sequences count separately)
The result fits within a 32-bit integer

examples.explanation: There are two ways: (1 step + 1 step) or (2 steps).

title: Fibonacci Number
description: The Fibonacci numbers form a sequence such that each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1. Given n, calculate F(n), where F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) for n > 1.
constraints: The result fits within a 32-bit integer

title: Minimum Cost Climbing Stairs
description: You are given an integer array cost where cost[i] is the cost of the ith step on a staircase. Once you pay the cost, you can either climb one or two steps. You can either start from the step with index 0 or the step with index 1. Return the minimum cost to reach the top of the floor (one step past the last index of the array).
constraints: You may start from index 0 or index 1
You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time

examples.explanation: You start at index 1, pay 15, and climb two steps to reach the top.
The cheapest path costs 6 by skipping the expensive steps.

title: Maximum Points from Line of Coins
description: Given an array nums representing values placed in a line, you may pick any subset of elements such that no two picked elements are adjacent in the array. Return the maximum possible sum of the picked elements.
constraints: No two adjacent elements can both be picked
An empty selection (sum 0) is allowed if all values are 0 or negative picks are avoided

examples.explanation: Picking elements 3, 5, and 7 gives a sum of 15, and no two are adjacent.
Picking elements 5, 100, and 5 gives a sum of 110.

title: Count Ways to Reach a Target Sum
description: Given an integer n, count the number of distinct ways to reach exactly n using steps of size 1, 2, or 3 (order matters, so different sequences count separately). Return the total number of ways modulo 1000000007.
constraints: Order of steps matters (different sequences are counted separately)
